pre_registered.question: AI produces many candidate crystal structures. With a fixed budget of validation calculations, which structures are worth validating, and does the leaderboard metric pick the model that fills that budget with the most truly stable structures?
pre_registered.data: Matbench Discovery @ 6d587c184cdb4a4865dc0b15b04a5e6d77ed464f: WBM summary (256,963 structures; 215,488 unique prototypes), every model with a discovery prediction file
pre_registered.reproduction_level: re-score from published formation-energy predictions; no relaxation re-run
pre_registered.truth: DFT (MP2020-corrected) energy above the MP convex hull; a computational reference, not experiment
pre_registered.decision_setting: unique-prototype test set as the candidate pool; a validation budget of K structures chosen by lowest predicted hull distance

hypotheses_stated_before_running.H1: Among models, the ranking by F1 differs from the ranking by precision@1% (Spearman < 0.9).
hypotheses_stated_before_running.H2: For each model, precision@K as K shrinks from 10% to 0.1% either keeps rising, plateaus or falls. 'Falls' (Goodhart-like) is defined as precision@0.1% below precision@1% with the bootstrap interval of the difference below 0. No direction is assumed.
hypotheses_stated_before_running.H3: Precision and recall are lower for candidates whose structure type (prototype label without elements) is rare or absent in the 2023 Materials Project snapshot.

boundaries.structure_type_novelty: count of the bare prototype label (protostructure_spglib before ':') among Materials Project entries in the 2023-02-07 snapshot used by the benchmark: 0, 1-9, >=10
boundaries.near_hull: |DFT hull distance| <= 0.05 eV/atom vs further away

pre_registered.display_models: the 10 best by unique-prototype F1, plus older baselines present in the data (Voronoi RF, CGCNN, MEGNet, BOWSR, CHGNet, M3GNet, MACE-MP-0)
pre_registered.bootstrap: structures resampled with replacement, 500 resamples, K taken as a fraction of the resample; seed 2026
limits: WBM candidates come from element substitution on known MP structures, so most are near known prototypes
truth is DFT, not synthesis or measurement
precision@K treats every validation as equal cost

post_hoc_additions: Structure-type novelty also computed with an element-order-invariant label (the bare label renames the same type when substitution changes the alphabetical order of elements), and from the INITIAL (pre-relaxation) structure, which is known at screening time. The pre-registered bare relaxed-label version is kept.

The pre-registered near-hull bin uses the TRUE DFT hull distance, which is unknown before validation. Added: bands of PREDICTED hull distance per model, where the 1%-budget picks fall, and the true hull distance of each false positive.
Bootstrap changed to a cluster bootstrap by chemical system (WBM structures come in correlated substitution families); intervals are conditional on this set of models.
Wasted share of a 1% budget (1 - precision) reported per model.
Better-half Spearman (models with F1 at or above the median) is exploratory, not a pre-registered hypothesis.
Base rates reported with both the rounded reference (leaderboard classification convention) and unrounded hull distances.
